name: Rust orange
lede: Rust orange is a deep orange named for oxidised iron; a real paint called by this name turns up in a famous American painter's paint box.

sections.title: Iron's orange
sections.body: The name takes its picture from [[rust]]. Ridgway recorded it in 1912, and ISCC-NBS 1955 files it under deep orange [2]. Close relatives are [[orange]], [[sienna]] and [[mars-orange]] [2].

sections.title: In Winslow Homer's paint box
sections.body: In the Pigment Compendium, mars yellow, essentially iron oxide hydroxide, can be roasted to produce a range of colors through oranges to reds [1]. Newman and colleagues in 1980 tentatively identified mars orange in a paint box owned by Winslow Homer, labelled rust orange and adulterated with calcite [1]. Chalk adulteration also appears in the records of the Amsterdam materials firm Claus and Fritz [1]. So the name was a real tube label, not only a swatch word [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive it appears in 0.69% of paintings (163), most often as an accent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1300s at 2.2 times the expected rate, and is over-represented in Indian paintings, at 4 times [3].
